server.instructions: Make and edit music in a live FL Studio session: use the run tool (Python with the fl SDK); its description is the manual.

trial.run_description:
Run Python in a persistent kernel, like a notebook cell; this is the only
tool, so everything is code. Variables and imports persist. The working
directory is your workspace, the one place you can write (files last for the
session); open(), subprocess, `!cmd` and `%pip install pkg` work, and the
internet is reachable. Pre-bound: fl, Note, theory, display; a trailing
expression is repr'd. Installed: numpy, scipy, soundfile, librosa,
matplotlib, pyloudnorm, mido, music21, Pillow.

Returns {outcome, stdout, result | traceback, actions, images}; actions says
what FL did, one sentence per change, even if the cell failed. outcome is ok,
error, interrupted (the run took its 600 s budget, fl calls included: stopped
between fl calls, variables kept; an fl call that would not fit, such as a
long render, is refused before it starts, so split long work across runs) or
kernel_lost (variables gone, files kept). Images show like a notebook's: end
with a matplotlib figure or PIL image, call display(...), or leave figures
open; at most 4 per run, about width x height / 750 tokens each.

Good to know:
- print(fl.scene()) shows the whole project in one digest: patterns, channels, playlist and mixer.
- You hear by measuring: fl.meters() takes seconds, a render plays in real time.

fl: The live FL Studio session: every call applies to FL at once and returns the result, or raises with the reason. Notes, playlist clips, automation clips and the project's notes are read from the song FL opened plus the edits made through fl, so changes to them in FL's own windows are not seen until FL saves the song; everything else is read from FL live. A channel is its index, exact name or a unique part of its name. help(fl.render) gives a member's arguments, defaults, results and limits.
  Read     scene(...) tempo channels mixer playlist patterns
  Notes    track(name_or_index, ...) track.write(notes, ...) track.notes() track.clear() Note(key, start, length, ...) theory.chord(root, ...) theory.scale(root, ...) theory.drums(pattern, ...) theory.transpose(notes, semitones) theory.quantize(notes, ...)
  Sound    sounds(...) audition(preset, ...) load_sample(channel, sample) load_preset(channel, preset) presets(channel) set_preset(channel, preset) track.params(...) track.set_param(param, value)
  Mix      track.set_levels(...) route(channel, mixer_track) send(src_track, dst_track, ...) effect(mixer_track, slot) effect.params(...) effect.set_param(param, value)
  Song     set_tempo(bpm) new_pattern(name, ...) rename_pattern(pattern, name) place(pattern, bars) automate(points, bar, ...)
  Hear     meters(...) render(output, ...) read_wav(path)
  Project  undo()
  Guides   guide(...)

Guides: optional reference, not instructions, each with a worked example. fl.guide("arrangement") prints one:
  arrangement  Optional reference on how patterns, the playlist and automation work here.
  chops        Optional reference on editing a sample in Python and playing it.
  listening    Optional reference on measuring a render, since you cannot hear playback.
  mixing       Optional reference on setting levels, sends, effects and panning from code.
  sidechain    Optional reference on ducking a part under the kick from code.
  sounds       Optional reference on searching, auditioning and loading sounds.

workspace_only.instructions: A Python workspace with no FL Studio session: use the run tool; its description says what it has.
